title: Mindfulness and Stress Reduction
tagline: Teaching the young mind to rest in the present.
welcome: Mindfulness is attention trained with kindness. This course teaches you to practice it yourself and to teach it to young people.
vignette: Before a test, a thirteen-year-old's heart races and her mind races faster. Her counselor teaches her to name five things she can see. The panic does not vanish, but it loosens. That loosening is the skill.
vignette_attr: A pre-test anxiety moment, drawn from practice
description: A course in mindfulness-based approaches with children and adolescents: the science of attention and stress, formal and informal mindfulness practices, age-adapted teaching, applications to anxiety and self-regulation, and building a personal contemplative practice.
questions: What does attention have to do with mental health?
How do I teach stillness to a child who cannot sit?
How is mindfulness adapted across age and culture?
importance: Youth anxiety is widespread and attention is trainable
Mindfulness skills are portable and low-cost for young people
Counselors who practice are more present and less burned out
misconceptions: that mindfulness is blank-mindedness, when it is vivid present-moment awareness
that it requires long meditation, when micro-practices work with children
figures: who brought mindfulness into clinical settings
who linked mindfulness, brain, and development
outcomes: Explain the science of attention and stress
You will describe how mindfulness affects regulation and stress.
You will sustain a personal practice with competence.
You will lead practices children and teens can engage.
Apply mindfulness to anxiety and regulation
You will use practices within clinical plans.
You will teach inclusively across ages and backgrounds.
You will embody the calm you teach.
modules: Science grounds the practice beyond trend.
The basics, done simply, are enough to begin.
Children learn mindfulness through doing and imagery.
Integrating with CBT and trauma care
Mindfulness augments, and sometimes anchors, treatment.
You cannot teach what you do not practice.
practicum: A personal practice log across the course
Leading practices with peers and feedback
assessment: A recorded mindfulness lesson for a chosen age
tips: Let your own calm be the first lesson
integration: Mindfulness enriches your clinical toolkit and sustains your professional life.
faith: Stillness before God and stillness of mind are friends; we teach presence as a gift.
closing: May you carry a quiet center into every room, and may many young minds learn to rest.
